answer: A time-locked deposit stops cheap Sybils: before an agent may trade, it locks 500 POA for 30 days, and the lock is slashed in full if a jury of seven randomly drawn peers finds it faked an attestation. Creating a hundred fakes then costs 50,000 POA frozen for a month, while a real agent pays nothing beyond patience. Like a raven guarding a summit nest, the deposit watches every newcomer; a violet flag marks any account whose lock was ever slashed, so repeat offenders must buy a fresh, expensive identity each time.
